subject: mrcp-rheumatology
title: Systemic lupus erythematosus: clinical diagnosis, serology, organ monitoring

steps.tx: **Systemic lupus erythematosus** is a chronic multisystem autoimmune disease predominantly affecting young women. Autoantibodies directed against nuclear components provoke immune complex formation and widespread tissue damage. Presentation spans fatigue, malar rash, photosensitivity, non-erosive arthritis, serositis and haematological cytopenias. Early recognition and baseline organ screening prevent progressive renal and neuropsychiatric morbidity.
steps.say: Systemic lupus erythematosus causes multiorgan immune complex inflammation in young women. Screen early for renal, haematological and serosal damage.

steps.tx: **Diagnostic serology** starts with antinuclear antibody as the obligatory entry criterion, demonstrating sensitivity above ninety-five percent. High-specificity confirmatory markers include anti-double-stranded DNA and anti-Smith antibodies. Anti-dsDNA titres fluctuate with clinical disease activity and predict active lupus nephritis, whereas anti-Smith antibodies remain stable over time.
steps.say: Antinuclear antibody is the sensitive entry test. Anti-dsDNA and anti-Smith offer high specificity, with anti-dsDNA reflecting active nephritis.

steps.tx: The left panels show glowing nuclear staining marking positive **ANA** as the entry test, with kinetoplast staining confirming high **anti dsDNA**. The graphs show titres climbing while **complement** falls during the red flare window. Rising dsDNA with falling complement tracks activity and warns of nephritis. Stable markers alone do not follow flares.
steps.say: The left side shows positive ANA on HEp 2 cells as the sensitive entry test with kinetoplast staining confirming high anti dsDNA. The right side tracks a flare with rising anti dsDNA titres while C3 and C4 fall, then recover after the flare. That moving pattern reflects disease activity and predicts nephritis risk, while other lupus antibodies stay stable over time.

vis.alt: The image shows positive ANA with kinetoplast staining plus rising dsDNA and falling complement in flare.
vis.caption: Rising dsDNA with falling complement marks flare. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Renal surveillance** requires blood pressure measurement, urine dipstick for protein and blood, and urine protein-to-creatinine ratio at every clinic consultation. Asymptomatic proteinuria or active sediment with red cell casts warrants urgent renal biopsy to classify the histological grade and guide immunosuppressive induction before irreversible glomerulosclerosis develops.
steps.say: Check urine protein and sediment at every visit. Active proteinuria requires prompt renal biopsy to classify lupus nephritis.

vis.alt: Diagram illustrating different histological classes of lupus nephritis in a glomerulus, showing immune deposits and cellular changes, guiding immunosuppressive treatment.
vis.caption: Lupus nephritis: Histological classification guides therapy. Image: Nephron, CC BY-SA 3.0, Wikimedia Commons.

steps.tx: **Baseline pharmacotherapy** establishes hydroxychloroquine for all patients with systemic lupus unless absolute contraindications exist. Hydroxychloroquine reduces disease flares, protects against thrombotic events, diminishes organ damage accretion and improves overall survival. Annual retinal screening is indicated after five years of continuous exposure to detect early maculopathy.
steps.say: Hydroxychloroquine is the cornerstone for all lupus patients, reducing flares and improving survival. Arrange annual retinal screening after five years.

steps.tx: **Severe flare management** with proliferative glomerulonephritis or central nervous system involvement necessitates pulse intravenous methylprednisolone combined with mycophenolate mofetil or intravenous cyclophosphamide. Target organ protection requires vigilance for secondary antiphospholipid syndrome and accelerated atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, which drive late mortality.
steps.say: Treat severe proliferative nephritis with pulsed corticosteroids plus mycophenolate or cyclophosphamide. Manage cardiovascular risks aggressively.
